title: Tandem Processor: Grappling with Emerging Operators in Neural Networks
problem: Conventional NPU designs inadequately support the growing diversity of non-GEMM operators in neural networks, instead relying on either dedicated blocks or general-purpose processor fallbacks. Despite the architectural importance of emerging operators, especially in language models, they have been disproportionately overlooked compared to GEMM operations.
motivation: As deep learning has evolved toward language models, non-GEMM operators have grown in diversity and complexity, interweaving with GEMM operations in structural patterns that require rethinking of neural acceleration beyond traditional NPU designs.
method: Modern neural networks need two kinds of operations: GEMM (matrix multiplication, the fast core operation) and diverse emerging operators (like attention and normalization, especially critical in language models). Traditional NPU designs either build isolated dedicated hardware for these emerging operators or make you fall back to slow general-purpose processors. The Tandem Processor instead integrates both operation types into a single unified architecture that can handle them efficiently together.
key_novelty: The Tandem Processor handles diverse emerging neural operators (like attention and normalization) natively within a single unified architecture, rather than using isolated dedicated blocks or forcing fallback to general-purpose processors.
contributions: Identifies and quantifies the inadequacy of GEMM-centric NPU designs for modern neural workloads
Proposes the Tandem Processor architecture for integrated support of diverse emerging operators
Demonstrates patterns of GEMM and non-GEMM operator interweaving in neural networks
primary_theme: Rethinking neural acceleration for diverse operators beyond GEMM
